prompt:
Output exactly one concise, information‑dense caption: a single grammatical sentence of comma‑separated short phrases. Use digits for counts; do not infer, hedge, paraphrase, or add anything not visually present. Output nothing else.

Required phrase ordering (include an item only if visually verifiable; omit unverifiable items). Aim for ≤30 words; allow up to +10% length only to include a fully legible quoted text string or one necessary part‑level relation/background anchor.

1) Start with: [digit] + subject noun(s) + spatial anchor.
   - Deterministic spatial rule: compute subject centroid x; if x < 0.33 → "left"; if 0.33 ≤ x ≤ 0.66 → "center"; if x > 0.66 → "right".
   - If subject width >60% image width, emit "center" regardless of centroid.
   - If >5% of subject area lies outside image, append "partially cropped at [top|bottom|left|right]".
   - Add depth token [foreground|midground|background] only if clear from overlap/relative scale; otherwise omit.

2) Immediately after, include exactly one visible micro‑action/part phrase if any of these verifiable cues is present: visible limb‑object contact, object held in hand, visible deformation/pressure, object midair/off ground, clear gaze at a visible object, or motion blur on a limb. Use one of these templates only:
   - "[hand] [verb] [object]" (e.g., "right hand holding pole")
   - "holding [object] with [hand]" (e.g., "holding violin with chin and right hand")
   - "[body_part] [verb] [structure/object]" (e.g., "left foot on pedal")
   If none apply, include exactly "no-action-visible".

3) Then include up to 1–3 high‑signal descriptor(s) chosen by strict priority (pick highest‑ranked verifiable candidates, break ties lexicographically):
   A) Legible text — transcribe exact string only if every character is clearly readable; include it in quotes and localize (e.g., "'LOEWE' on lower sill at left").
   B) Reflection/surface condition (e.g., "wet pavement with reflections", "glass reflections").
   C) Material/texture (e.g., "rusted metal", "woven straw").
   D) Distinctive accessory (e.g., "white hard hat", "red pennant").
   E) Color (e.g., "red sweatshirt").
   - Enforce ≤3 descriptors; if none verifiable, omit descriptors.

4) If a person/object clearly interacts with another object/structure, include exactly one concise part‑level relation phrase using the template: "[part] [verb] [object/structure]" (e.g., "right hand holding pole", "rear wheel off ground"). Include this only if contact/displacement is visually evident.

5) Optionally include exactly one viewpoint token when obvious: {close-up, medium, wide, high-angle, low-angle}.

6) Optionally include exactly one lighting token when obvious: {backlit, front-lit, rim-lit, long-shadow-left, long-shadow-right}.

7) If a clear background anchor is visible, append one concise background noun phrase (single phrase, e.g., "storefront window", "stone embankment", "Radio City marquee"). Omit if no clear anchor.

Reflections vs. behind‑glass rule
- If an element appears doubled, reversed, or overlayed on the glass plane without 3D occlusion → label as "reflections".
- If objects clearly sit on the far side of the glass (shelf, mannequin, handbags) → label as "on display behind glass" or "behind glass".
- If uncertain, omit both.

Two‑pass verification (must run before emitting):
a) Transcribe quoted text only if every character is readable; otherwise drop text token.
b) Include a digit count only if each instance is clearly visible and ≥50% unobstructed; otherwise omit count.
c) Include depth only if overlap/relative scale is unambiguous.
d) Include "partially cropped" only if >5% of subject area is outside image.
e) Drop any token failing verification and recheck sentence for grammaticality.

Brevity & prioritization
- If length limits force removal, prioritize tokens in this order: legible text → part‑level relation → background anchor → descriptors → viewpoint → lighting.
- Use compact, active, factual phrasing and concrete nouns. Do not infer ages, emotions, roles, intent, or unseen attributes. Do not use vague quantifiers ("several","many") — use digits only when clear.

Style constraints
- Single sentence, comma‑separated short phrases, no tags, no lists, no extra lines.
- Use canonical labels (e.g., "storefront window", "center"), consistent punctuation for quoted text.

Canonical good examples (follow exact output format):
- "1 child left foreground, reaching toward storefront window, right hand touching glass, 'LOEWE' on lower sill at left, glass reflections, storefront window behind."
- "1 woman center foreground, holding violin with chin and right hand, open instrument case on ground, medium, tiled underground passage behind."
- "1 surfer center midground, crouching on surfboard, sharp turn with spray arc behind, sunlit green wave face, low-angle, ocean behind."
- "5 dancers center foreground, standing in long line across crosswalk, red and white striped costumes, Radio City marquee above, street behind."

Follow these rules exactly to produce one precise caption.
